regenerable_on: a lab guest with OpenZFS installed and the brimful staging: a 1 GiB file-backed pool carrying a quota-bounded dataset filled past the warn line, a dataset with snapshot churn (write, snapshot, rewrite), a canmount=noauto dataset, a readonly=on dataset, a local-mountpoint dataset with a child that INHERITS it, and defaults everywhere else.
note: storage/datasets' first committed pair, staged so every property surface the collection reads is a real value: use percentage under a QUOTA (headroom is quota-bounded, not pool-bounded), snapshot-held bytes from genuine churn, all three mountpoint source shapes (default, local, inherited-naming-its-ancestor), canmount=noauto with mounted=no beside it, and readonly=on stored — not masked, because the capture ran unsandboxed; the ProtectSystem mask is the Go collector's unit-tested branch and the reference's recorded audit. The pool itself also rides the payloads as the corpus's first FILE-vdev pool, unrequested by this variant's collections.
coverage_note: What this variant does not reach: ReadOnlyUnobservable (the ProtectSystem=strict mask needs a sandboxed reader, so the fact is exercised by the collector's own unit tests and named in corpus.NAMED_RESIDUALS with that venue), a received property source, and volumes/bookmarks — every staged dataset is a filesystem.
anchors_note: Transcribed from the scrubbed zfs-list.json (the staged name brimful was substituted to host-5797a2, consistently through keys, paths and the inherited source's data). tight: used 61948928 of a 67108864 quota leaves avail 5159936, and 61948928*100/67108864 = 92.31 → 92 under the half-even rounding both implementations share — inside the warn band, so the dataset-capacity rule fires warn and not critical. data's snapshot bytes are the 8 MiB blob rewritten after snapshotting. kid's mountpoint source names the ancestor it inherits from; custom's is local; everything else is DEFAULT, rendered as the word default — only NONE and an absent source render as no statement.
